description.narrative: The Project Development Objective is to promote private investments and firm growth in non-resource based sectors.

The objective of the Ghana Economic Transformation Project is to promote private investments and firm growth in non-resource-based sectors. This project has four components. Component (1) - Enabling investments, will focus on improving the enabling business environment, investment attraction capacity and the quality infrastructure support system for companies that want to invest and grow their businesses in Ghana. Component (2) - Crowding-in investments: Promoting spatial and industrial planning and development, will focus on enhancing the Government's programs in investment promotion and spatial development (including Special Economic Zones), thereby addressing the constraint to access quality industrial land in the country. Component (3) - Accelerating Entrepreneurship and MSME growth, will support entrepreneurship and MSME growth in non-resource-based sectors, addressing specifically the limited development of the MSME and entrepreneurship support ecosystem, including early stage financing. Component (4) – Project Management and Evaluation, will finance project management activities including fiduciary responsibilities, procurement, communication and dissemination, as well as monitoring and evaluation of project implementation and its impact. This will include capacity building for the Project Coordinating Unit (PCU), the Economic Transformation Unit and the Resource Mobilization and Economic Relations Division (RMERD) within the Ministry of Finance (MOF).

title.narrative: Improvement in investor perception of GIPC performance

comment.narrative: The first Investor Perception Survey report, completed in April 2024, established a baseline aggregate perception index of 28 out of 100 for Ghana's investment climate among both existing and potential investors. The baseline GIPC Performance Index, based on feedback from existing investors, scored 9 out of 100. The next survey round, expected after deployment of the CRM system and other investor servicing tools, will determine the level of improvement against the 2025 target.

title.narrative: Improvement in investor perception of GIPC performance

comment.narrative: The first Investor Perception Survey, completed in April 2024, established a baseline perception index of 28/100 for Ghana's investment climate and a GIPC Performance Index of 9/100. No update has been recorded since. The next survey round is expected to be undertaken after GIPC has substantially implemented actions such as the rollout of the CRM and other interventions to improve investor experience and stakeholder perception.

title.narrative: Increase (additional) in average value of gross sales by firms supported by the project

comment.narrative: Achieved: From the firm perspective, which measures the average percentage change in gross sales per SME, the project achieved a weighted average increase of 16.8% across all five (5) grant interventions based on inflation-adjusted data from a sample of 510 SMEs out of a population of 1,345. This indicates that, on average, beneficiary SMEs recorded real growth in sales, one year following project support, though the magnitude varied by intervention. Youth and Enterprise Growth SMEs showed the strongest average gains (24-25%), followed by COVID-19 grant II (18.01%) while women-owned SMEs grant program experienced modest increases (3%). The PwD-owned SMEs grant, however, recorded a decline (-3%). The overall positive weighted average underscores that the project has broadly contributed to improved firm-level performance among beneficiaries, despite heterogeneous outcomes reflecting differences in business capacity, market exposure, and intensity of technical support.

title.narrative: Increase (additional) in average value of gross sales by firms supported by the project

comment.narrative: An outcome assessment of 157 out of 413 SMEs supported under the COVID-19 Response Grant (Phase II) showed an average increase of 18.01% in real gross sales one year after receiving support. While results varied across firms, this performance aligns with the grant's objective of mitigating the economic effects of COVID-19 and suggests progress toward achieving the 2025 end-target. Data collection is ongoing for other grant programs, including the Enterprise Grow Program and support to women-, youth-, and PWD-owned firms, to provide a more comprehensive update.

title.narrative: Increase in number of QI services delivered

comment.narrative: Achieved. The equipment supplied by the GETP to the GSA has played a significant role in laboratory operations, contributing to approximately 50% of the total tests conducted (637 out of 1,283) from 2022 through August 2024. Additionally, of the 699 weighbridge truck services provided, 458 services (66%) utilized the GETP-supplied weighbridge truck as of April 24, 2025

title.narrative: Number of SMEs benefitting from capacity upgrading support

comment.narrative: Achieved. The project has exceeded its target for the number of SMEs benefitting from capacity upgrading support. As of December 2024, a total of 2,328 SMEs, under the Enterprise Grow Program have received basic business management training, surpassing the end-target of 2,000 SMEs. Of these, 748 SMEs (inclusive of pilot cohorts) have completed 360-degree diagnostics, while 516 SMEs have received full capacity upgrade support. The remainder are at various stages of technical assistance. To sustain this progress and meet final targets across disaggregated categories, it is recommended that the Cohort 4 randomization process—which determines capacity upgrade modalities—be expedited.

title.narrative: Number of SMEs benefitting from capacity upgrading support

comment.narrative: Achieved. The project has trained 2,329 Enterprise Grow firms in basic business management. Of these, 950 (pilot inclusive) firms have completed 360 diagnostics, and 742 (pilot excluded) firms have received full capacity upgrading support. Total number of firms that have received “full capacity upgrade (inclusive of pilot)” is therefore 765. The remaining firms are at various stages of technical assistance, including 360 diagnostics, and business management training. To expedite progress towards the target, the cohort 4 randomization process determining the type of capacity upgrades each firm receives should be fast-tracked.

title.narrative: Beneficiaries satisfied with quality of services provided by the project

comment.narrative: The project achieved an overall weighted beneficiary satisfaction rating of 97.3% in an internal assessment. Satisfaction among TIAs and VCTF-supported fund managers was 100%, GEA grantees 98%, and GKICP Project-Affected Persons (PAPs) 86% (based on GRM data). The results reflect strong stakeholder engagement and service delivery, though the lower satisfaction among GKICP PAPs, linked to one court case and valuation concerns from 7 PAPs and the traditional authority calls for continued dialogue and resolution efforts.

title.narrative: Number of new systems and tools deployed for improved investor servicing

comment.narrative: GIPC has completed one system and is in the advanced stages of finalizing two additional tools to enhance investor servicing. The Customer Relationship Management (CRM) system has been developed and user training conducted; however, it remains undeployed due to hosting issues with NITA. GIPC and the PCU plan to engage NITA to resolve the issue and are also exploring alternative hosting options and financing solutions. The IT procurement budget for GIPC also increased significantly—from USD 155,000 to USD 700,000—prompting concerns about value-for-money. A web-based Monitoring & Evaluation (M&E) system is also near completion, with pre-testing ongoing.

title.narrative: Number of Conformity Assessment Bodies Assessed or Accredited

comment.narrative: A total of seven Conformity Assessment Bodies (CABs) have been assessed by the Ghana Accreditation Service (GHAS) since 2022. These include Everpro Ltd (calibration lab), QCC (COCOBOD) Pesticide Residue Lab, Patholab Solutions Ltd, Quadushah Medical Diagnostic Centre, M&G Clinical Laboratory Ltd, Bill Clinical, and Gold Crest Refinery Laboratories. Of these, the QCC Pesticide Residue Lab has been accredited, while the remaining six are actively working toward meeting accreditation requirements. The project remains on track to achieve the 2025 end-target of 10 assessed or accredited CABs.

title.narrative: Number of Conformity Assessment Bodies Assessed or Accredited

comment.narrative: Since 2022, GHAS has assessed seven Conformity Assessment Bodies (CABs) as part of efforts to strengthen national quality infrastructure and promote compliance with international standards. These include Everpro Ltd (calibration lab), QCC (COCOBOD) Pesticide Residue Lab, Patholab Solutions Ltd (medical lab), Quadushah Medical Diagnostic Centre, M&G Clinical Laboratory Ltd, Bill Clinical, and Gold Crest Refinery Laboratories. title.narrative: Time to resolve commercial disputes at district courts

comment.narrative: Stalled. The planned District Court Case Management System under GETP has been discontinued due to budget and time constraints. The only responsive bid exceeded the US$1.8 million allocation by over three times, and the proposed implementation timeline extended beyond the project's June 2026 closure. Consequently, progress tracking on PDO Indicator #2 (commercial dispute resolution turnaround time in pilot districts) has stalled, and the recommendation has been to drop the activity and indicator in the subsequent restructuring. The baseline turnaround time was updated to 178 days based on six pilot courts selected for their commercial caseload, structural readiness, and digital infrastructure.

title.narrative: Time to resolve commercial disputes at district courts

comment.narrative: This indicator will need to be dropped, as the court case management system that underpins it will not be implemented. Although the procurement process progressed to the evaluation stage, the financial proposal exceeded the allocated budget by more than four times. Furthermore, the projected implementation timeline now goes beyond the project's scheduled closure date, rendering the activity unfeasible within the remaining period.

title.narrative: Time to obtain a construction permit

comment.narrative: The GETP has successfully achieved its 2025 target of reducing the average construction permit turnaround time in the Greater Accra Region to 50 days, down from a baseline of 83 days in 2022. This progress reflects a sustained and steady improvement—66 days by mid-2023, 61 days by the end of 2023, and 50 days by Q3 2024—based on a revised methodology that includes only data from the 13 MMDAs that consistently reported throughout the period, along with input from the Lands Commission, Fire Service, and EPA. Provisional data from Q4 2024 indicate a further decline to 46 days. These gains are attributed to GETP-supported institutional reforms, including enhanced IT infrastructure for relevant agencies and regular oversight through steering committees and performance reviews led by the Ministry of Trade, Agribusiness, and Industry.

title.narrative: Time to obtain a construction permit

comment.narrative: The average construction/development permit turnaround time in Greater Accra reduced significantly from 83 days in 2022 to 53 days in 2024, reflecting improvements in efficiency and coordination among key permitting institutions. The turnaround days, which was previously reported as 50 days, have been revised to 53 days following the Data Quality Audit jointly conducted by the PCU, MoTAI-BRR, and the OHLGS in April 2025.
